subject: Model-fit eval & next steps (open models vs PayGrid proprietary baseline)
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Alice Morgan <alice@paygrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed model-fit eval + next steps

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and really helpful context on PayGrid's primary objectives for Q3. Quick recap from our side and a proposed plan to evaluate parity with your current proprietary baseline:

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: move chat/agent routing to a cheaper, high-quality open-model stack while matching intent and correctness at production load.
- Acceptance criteria: intent accuracy >= 95% on core billing workflows, no more than a 2% regression in downstream NPS for top-10 flows.
- Constraints: 99th pctl latency target <= 500ms for short-turn queries; retention & audit logs must meet SOC2 requirements.

Redwood proposal (next steps)
1) Model-fit eval: Redwood will run a parity eval comparing your current baseline vs recommended open models on the prompt set you shared.
   - Recommended candidates: Llama2-70B-Q4 (high-quality baseline), OpenLlama-13B-8k-quant (cost-efficient), RedW-13B-int8 (our optimized 8-bit profile).
2) Deliverables: benchmark PDF (latency/cost/accuracy), prompt-set results CSV, eval run notes, and a recap meeting to review thresholds and go/no-go.
3) Timeline: 5 business days to run initial parity tests once we have final prompt set + access to sample logs.

Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.txt (your sample prompts), and we'll attach our internal benchmark summary once runs complete.

Questions for you
- Can you confirm the acceptance thresholds above (intent accuracy / NPS regression / latency)?
- Confirm we can use the provided anonymized sample logs for metric calibration (or provide a sanitized export).
- Any restrictions on storing eval artifacts in Redwood-managed S3 for the duration of the test?

If that looks good, I'll have Marissa kick off the eval and share the Drive folder + HubSpot update (deal PG-2027-042). Proposed time for the review session: next Thu 4/29 11am PT.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.txt (20 prompts, billing/customer-support intent sets)

From: Alice Morgan <alice@paygrid.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@paygrid.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed model-fit eval + next steps

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Acceptance thresholds: intent accuracy target is 95%+ for the top-12 billing intents. The 2% NPS regression is fine as a threshold — we'll validate with product on tolerances for edge flows.
- Latency: can we measure both P50 and P95? P50 is less critical; P95 <= 500ms is the non-negotiable.
- Data: we can provide an anonymized sample export (10k interactions) — I'll have procurement coordinate the sanitized S3 link.

Couple of asks:
1) Can Redwood run A/B tests (open model vs our current on-prem baseline) and provide per-intent confusion matrices? That's critical for product to sign off.
2) On regressions: do you have tooling for quick rollback or automatic fallback to baseline if we see regression in production?

If you can confirm those two items, we can proceed. Meeting time for 4/29 11am PT works for me.

Best,
Alice
Head of Product, PayGrid
alice@paygrid.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alice Morgan <alice@paygrid.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed model-fit eval + next steps

Hi Alice / Lauren —

Thanks — Marissa here, I'll own the eval execution and reporting. Quick answers and the proposed technical plan: 

Answers to your asks
- A/B testing: yes — we can run side-by-side inference runs on the same prompt set and produce per-intent confusion matrices, precision/recall, and aggregated intent accuracy. We'll produce both CSVs and a summary PDF.
- Rollback/fallback: Redwood supports automatic model routing policies. If you deploy and enable the "parity-fallback" policy, traffic will fail over to your baseline variant when model-level quality or latency SLOs are breached. We can demo during the review.

Technical plan (high-level)
1) Baselines to test:
   - PayGrid proprietary baseline (you provide inference samples or an evaluation endpoint)
   - Llama2-70B-Q4 (high-quality open candidate)
   - OpenLlama-13B-8k-quant (cost-efficient candidate)
   - RedW-13B-int8 (Redwood-optimized quantized profile)
2) Metrics we will deliver: per-intent accuracy, confusion matrix, BLEU/ROUGE-style text overlap for scripted responses, P50/P95 latency, and per-token cost estimates.
3) Data handling: we will use the sanitized S3 export you provide. All artifacts for the eval will be stored in a temporary Redwood-managed folder (we'll keep for 30 days unless you request deletion).
4) Timeline: kick off Friday 4/23, initial results by 4/28, review 4/29 (11am PT).

Attachments included: redwood_benchmark_summary_20270421.pdf (initial microbenchmarks on the candidate models), eval_run_notes_20270422.csv (planned eval matrix + prompts mapping). Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-paygrid-evals (we will populate this folder with results).

Next steps for PayGrid
- Confirm acceptance thresholds (Alice confirmed intent accuracy & P95 latency).
- Provide sanitized S3 export or a temporary read-only eval endpoint.
- Grant HubSpot view access for Marissa so we can update PG-2027-042 with the evaluation stage (I'll ping Sales Ops).

I'll start the runs as soon as we have the sanitized data. Thanks — excited to help get this across the line.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
